evidence.quote: the canal was never completed as envisioned, as the American Civil War (1861-1865) interrupted construction above Lynchburg and by then, railroads were becoming more numerous and popular.

evidence.claim: In 1880, the canal passed to a new railway company, which began laying tracks along it.
evidence.quote: the James River and Kanawha Canal was conveyed to a new railroad company by a deed dated March 4, 1880.

evidence.claim: The James and Rivanna meet at Columbia, formerly called Point of Fork.
evidence.quote: Columbia, formerly known as Point of Fork, is a village and census designated place in Fluvanna County, Virginia, United States, at the confluence of the James and Rivanna rivers.

evidence.claim: That junction linked Richmond and Lynchburg by the James and Charlottesville by the Rivanna.
evidence.quote: The confluence of the rivers at Columbia linked Richmond to Lynchburg through the James River and to Charlottesville through the Rivanna.

evidence.claim: Columbia developed a bateau freight line for the tobacco trade and later became a stagecoach stop between Richmond and Staunton.
evidence.quote: Columbia became a shipping point on the James River for Virginia's tobacco trade, establishing its own bateau freight line.

evidence.claim: Passenger rail service ended in 1958; floods from Hurricanes Camille and Agnes destroyed homes and businesses in 1969 and 1972.
evidence.quote: The town entered an economic decline with the end of passenger railroad service in 1958, and saw many homes and businesses destroyed in floods caused by Hurricanes Camille in 1969 and Agnes in 1972.

evidence.claim: After a resident referendum, Columbia ceased to be an incorporated town in 2016.
evidence.quote: The disincorporation took effect on July 1, 2016.

evidence.claim: Goochland’s other name, Goochland Court House, identifies its role as the county seat just north of the James.

evidence.claim: Dabney Cosby built the courthouse in 1826 as a two-story brick building with a temple form and a projecting Tuscan portico.
evidence.quote: The Goochland County Court House was built in 1826 by Dabney Cosby, an architect of the area. It is a two-story, temple-form brick structure with a projecting pedimented tetrastyle Tuscan order portico.
